title: Portland rally encourages voting in midterm elections on No Kings Day

tea.why: Protesters gathered to encourage early voting and rally support for Democratic candidates ahead of the midterm elections.
tea.want: Participants want to elect Maine Democrats, oust Republican incumbent Susan Collins, and ensure democratic representation.
tea.changed: Oct 17, 2026: About 400 people gathered in Deering Oaks for a No Kings Day rally featuring speeches from Democratic candidates and officials.

summary: Around 400 people gathered at Deering Oaks park in Portland, Maine, on Saturday for a rally organized by Indivisible Greater Portland. The event coincided with the fourth national No Kings day and focused on encouraging voters to cast ballots early in the upcoming midterm elections, supporting Maine Democrats, and removing five-term Republican incumbent Susan Collins from the U.S. Senate. Speakers included Democratic gubernatorial candidate Hannah Pingree, U.S. Senate candidate Troy Jackson, and U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren. Speakers criticized President Donald Trump and Senator Collins, addressing issues such as healthcare, immigration, abortion, and affordability challenges. No official response or actions by authorities were reported in the sources.
demands: Defeat Susan Collins in the U.S. Senate race
Encourage early voting in the midterm elections
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: About 400 people gathered at Deering Oaks in Portland for a No Kings Day rally supporting Democratic candidates.
